title: Pin core.quotePath=false per git command, not via repo config
context: Git's default core.quotePath=true octal-quotes non-ASCII paths (café.ts → caf\303\251.ts). Path enumerations returned spellings that mismatched stored POSIX paths and constraint globs, causing files to silently evade CI gates and metrics to read zero.
decision: Explicitly pin core.quotePath=false on all 10 git path-enumeration calls using `-c core.quotePath=false`, ensuring paths are always returned as literal UTF-8 independent of repo configuration.
consequences: Encoding normalization happens at the git boundary, not downstream or in the store
System is resilient to missing or misconfigured repo-level quotePath settings
Files with non-ASCII names no longer silently evade constraint scopes and metrics
Pattern established for all future path enumeration code
alternatives_rejected: Set core.quotePath=false repo-wide in config (hides intent, relies on setup, doesn't catch missing config)
Post-process git output to convert octal-quoted paths (adds downstream complexity, inconsistency risk)
Accept encoding inconsistency and patch only downstream consumers (fragile, incomplete)
